Returning NaN for a negative index with unknown size should trigger slice’s size-resolution path instead of treating the index as zero. That likely fixes filtered finite ranges, though the patch includes no regression test.

An unknown size previously converted a negative index to 0, explaining why the slice was ignored. Returning NaN should let the slice logic determine the filtered collection’s size before resolving the index.

With an unknown size, a negative slice index currently resolves to zero, effectively ignoring the slice. Returning NaN should trigger the existing path that caches the sequence to determine its size before resolving the index.

Using collection.size fixes OrderedSet hashes when deleted entries leave internal gaps, addressing the reported inequality. However, collections with an unknown size previously used the iteration count; hashing them with undefined may introduce new equality/hash inconsistencies.

Using collection.size should fix hashes inflated by OrderedSet’s internal deletion gaps, restoring equality in the reported case. But collections with unknown size, such as some lazy Seqs, may now hash differently despite equal contents.
The empty-stack check returns the childless root once and marks the iterator exhausted, directly addressing the reported exception. Existing traversal logic remains unchanged for roots with children.
The exception identifies TextBlockLiteralExpr as unsupported. Returning the same String type used for ordinary string literals should let method resolution find String.formatted on text blocks.
The guard handles a childless root before peek(), returns the root once, and marks the iterator exhausted. Traversal of roots with children remains unchanged.

Text blocks have type java.lang.String. Adding this TypeExtractor visitor addresses the reported unsupported-expression exception and should allow the existing String method-resolution path to resolve formatted.

The exception identifies TextBlockLiteralExpr as unsupported during type extraction. Returning the same String type used for ordinary string literals should allow method resolution to find String.formatted.

The guard handles an empty stack by returning the childless root once and marking the iterator exhausted. It directly addresses the reported exception; behavior if next() is called after exhaustion remains uncertain.

The loop parses any number of `and`/`or` operators and links each comparison to the next, addressing the reported syntax error. It also preserves the existing behavior for zero or one operator.
The loop consumes every successive and/or operator and links each comparison as a child condition, addressing the reported parse error while preserving the existing two-comparison behavior.

The loop parses and links every subsequent `and` or `or` comparison, addressing the reported three-clause expression. Chaining child conditions also preserves Liquid’s right-to-left evaluation behavior.

The patch exposes the document’s filename through DocumentDrop, making page.name available in post templates. File.basename(path) matches the requested filename behavior; remaining risk is an untested interaction with existing post metadata.

Returning NaN for a negative index with unknown size should let slice detect that it must materialize the filtered sequence before resolving the index. The patch is plausible, though its success depends on that existing fallback.
The patch skips items only when they compare equal. It does not normalize relative and absolute source paths, so separate objects representing the same file may still trigger the reported conflict.

The loop parses and links arbitrarily many comparisons, directly addressing the reported error. Mixed and/or expressions may still have unexpected evaluation order, and the patch adds no tests for that case.
No patch was provided, so the duplicate-file conflict behavior remains unchanged.
The patch deduplicates file objects using equality, not normalized source paths. The relative and absolute paths likely belong to distinct objects, so the reported conflict would remain.
The patch exposes Document#basename as page.name, but basename omits the file extension. The reported expectation is the post’s filename, which Document#name appears to provide.

Posts use DocumentDrop, and exposing the document’s basename should make page.name return the post filename. The main uncertainty is whether Document#basename includes the extension expected by the docs.

The patch rejects the reported << Provides relation, but its regex also rejects valid package names containing dots or plus signs and accepts some invalid Debian versions. Hidden tests covering valid Provides may fail.

The patch sets empty packages’ default architecture to all, matching the request. Explicit architecture options applied after initialization should still work, though the result depends on output formats translating all appropriately.

The change makes empty packages default to architecture-independent output, addressing the reported behavior. It relies on output formats translating “all” appropriately; the patch itself does not show that path.

A nonempty NO_COLOR disables coloring as requested, but the unconditional check also overrides an explicit -C/--color flag. The NO_COLOR convention says per-invocation command-line options should take precedence.

The change lets `--` stop option parsing before the jq program, then treats subsequent arguments as positional. It preserves the existing behavior when `--` follows the program.

When validation.attributes is missing, the translator returns its key as a string. Casting it to an array lets the numeric parameter 0 resolve to that string. The patch skips that lookup while preserving valid attribute translations.

This fixes the reported example by falling back to the custom rule’s message when the attribute’s message array lacks that rule. Wildcard attribute message arrays can still be returned as arrays, leaving a similar failure unresolved.

The patch prevents an exact attribute’s nested messages from being treated as errors when a custom rule has no matching message. Wildcard attribute keys can still return the whole nested array, so related cases may remain broken.

The patch adds isSphere = true to every Sphere instance, matching the requested Box3-style type flag, and documents it. The reported check should now work.

The patch wraps ordinary ASCII paths, but uses byte lengths rather than display widths. Unicode paths can panic at split_at, and ANSI color codes can be split or cause incorrect wrapping. Narrow terminals can also underflow or loop indefinitely.

This likely fixes the reported merge with a default-fallback router. But it marks the outer router as having a custom fallback, so merging a router with a genuine outer fallback may now panic.

The patch uses Buf::chunks_vectored with poll_write_vectored when supported, retains the existing fallback, and advances the buffer by the reported byte count. Pending, partial writes, and write-zero handling appear correct.

Removing the last item now wakes a task waiting in poll_expired, allowing it to observe the empty queue. The change also covers clear; try_remove appears to use the same removal path.

The patch wakes the stored poller when removal empties the queue, allowing poll_expired to observe the empty state. It also covers clear; try_remove appears to use the same removal path.

The patch prevents an idle file from scheduling a zero-byte read, fixing the reported false EOF. It does not handle empty-buffer polls while a read is already in progress, which may still return Pending.

The option is configured as requiring a value, but --ignore-signal[=SIG] must work without one. Bare --ignore-signal may consume the program name or fail, and the empty-value path ignores no signals rather than all signals.
